name: Hosotani Universe
description: A closed universe filled with a homogeneous magnetic SU(2) gauge field, expanding from a curvature singularity and recollapsing.
convention: We use units $c=\hbar=1$, so cosmic time carries dimensions of length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Magnetic energy fills the round 3-spheres of Yutaka Hosotani's 1984 universe [hosotani1984]. He found an exact solution of the coupled Einstein-Yang-Mills equations with a homogeneous gauge field. Every comoving observer measures the same energy density and isotropic pressure. The spatial rotations act on the field together with internal gauge rotations [gibbons1994ym].¶The gauge group is $SU(2)$, whose group manifold is itself a 3-sphere. The spatial geometry therefore supplies a natural map into the gauge group. A single amplitude $f$ multiplies the invariant gauge connection. Hosotani's configuration has $f=1/2$, a purely magnetic solution between the pure gauge vacua at $f=0$ and $f=1$ [gibbons1994ym].¶As the universe expands, the magnetic strength falls as $a^{-2}$, where $a$ is the spatial radius. Its energy density $\rho$ falls as $a^{-4}$, and its pressure is $p=\rho/3$. The radius evolves as $a=\ell\sin\eta$, where $\eta$ is conformal time and $\ell$ is the maximum radius [gibbons1994ym]. In units with $c=\hbar=1$, the gravitational constant $G$ and gauge coupling $e$ fix $\ell^2=4\pi G/e^2$. Expansion ends at $a=\ell$, and contraction takes the universe to a second curvature singularity after a total cosmic lifetime of $2\ell$.¶The magnetic configuration rests at the top of the reduced gauge potential. Small homogeneous disturbances grow away from $f=1/2$, and Hosotani identified one unstable gauge mode [hosotani1984, gibbons1994ym]. The equilibrium concerns the gauge amplitude; the spatial radius expands and recollapses.¶Gary William Gibbons and Alan R. Steif investigated time dependent homogeneous gauge configurations in work published in 1994 [gibbons1994ym]. They followed the gauge amplitude between vacua with different winding numbers. For a massless fermion coupled to this gauge field, an energy level crosses zero as the amplitude passes through $f=1/2$. At the magnetic equilibrium, the corresponding fermion mode has zero energy.

related.text: A closed radiation cosmology with $a=\ell\sin\eta$, where $\eta$ is conformal time and $\ell$ is the maximum radius. A homogeneous $SU(2)$ magnetic field supplies the radiation stress [gibbons1994ym].
Conformal time separates the evolving radius from the round 3-sphere: $ds^2=a^2(-d\eta^2+d\Omega_3^2)$ [gibbons1994ym].

coordinates.name: Cosmic Hyperspherical

parameters.description: Maximum spatial radius, a positive length, with $\ell^2=4\pi G/e^2$ for gauge coupling $e$ and the fixed homogeneous $SU(2)$ amplitude $f=1/2$; the spatial radius is $a=\sqrt{t(2\ell-t)}=\ell\sin\eta$

coordinates.convention: We use cosmic time $t$ and angles $(\chi,\theta,\phi)$ on the round 3-sphere. A dot in the geodesic equations denotes a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Conformal Hyperspherical

parameters.description: Maximum spatial radius, a positive length, with $\ell^2=4\pi G/e^2$ for gauge coupling $e$ and the fixed homogeneous $SU(2)$ amplitude $f=1/2$; the spatial radius is $a=\sqrt{t(2\ell-t)}=\ell\sin\eta$

coordinates.convention: We use dimensionless conformal time $\eta$, with $t=\ell(1-\cos\eta)$ and angles $(\chi,\theta,\phi)$ on the round 3-sphere. A dot in the geodesic equations denotes a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
